source_scope: Frozen raw-lifetime extension submodule/tests and native fixture. Root integration supplies full-workspace dependency closure. No global ledger/inventory changes.

original_assertion_audit.current_change: No original test bodies or existing public DynamicArray algorithms changed. All52 mappings and every previous DynamicArray method/iterator/insertion/storage regression executed successfully.

public_declaration_bindings.scope: Detached raw AllocateOptimal; checked increment*item_size and existing allocator allocation-failure boundary
Raw nullable Free through current compatible allocator; not valid for registered typed AllocVec addresses
Explicit constructor closure writes to aligned exclusive uninitialized raw storage; does not publish ownership
Drop one exclusively owned live value removed from automatic ownership; no free or publication
Prevalidated initialized prefix; each Vec length and logical Size updated without drop or element moves
Only destination with zero allocated blocks; preserve or adopt allocator, copy stride and reset size

native_fixture.joined_columns: Size, registered block count, allocation/free counts and requested bytes, construction attempts and completed destructions, all published/restored values, allocator keep/adopt identities.
native_fixture.allocation_observation: Rust reads actual accumulating allocator live counts and free-space deltas at each allocation-only or free-only phase. Fixture uses a single arena block with aligned8/16-byte requests, so measured consumed bytes equal native requested bytes; no expected counters are injected.
native_fixture.parameter_probe_order: Native keep/adopt detached allocations coexist until the row prints; Rust observes and frees the independent keep allocation before the independent adopt allocation. Separate allocator identities and all recorded results are equal; simultaneous allocation lifetime is not claimed as a compared column.
native_fixture.defined_domain: Detached raw pointers use their allocating raw resource. Three typed-capacity slots are constructed before publication; shrink/restore does not destroy them. Removed values are manually destroyed only after shrinking ownership. Failed construction is never destroyed and is retried before raw free. No invalid native pointer/lifetime case is executed.

unsafe_ownership_contracts: Raw allocation/free uses BaseAllocator::allocate_optimal_raw/free_raw_nullable and never the typed AllocVec allocation path. The API explicitly prohibits raw-freeing a registered block_at pointer because typed heap provenance/layout differs.

construct_at requires aligned writable exclusive uninitialized storage; caller owns cleanup until publication. destroy_at requires a live value removed from automatic Drop ownership, with no conflicting aliases.

set_used_size checks logical available capacity and EVERY physical Vec capacity before changing ANY length. Validation failure does not require initialization preconditions and leaves metadata unchanged.

Successful publication requires valid fully initialized uniquely owned T values throughout the new prefix. Vec::set_len changes metadata only; shrink/restore preserves bytes and ends no value lifetime. Removed values need explicit cleanup or valid reconstruction/publication as documented.

copy_parameters rejects all destination allocations, including retained empty blocks, before changing allocator/stride/size. Existing detached pointers retain their original allocator requirements after parameter changes.

Unsafe code is confined to the small raw_lifetime submodule and annotated with safety reasons. All8 tests pass strict-provenance Miri with normal leak checks, without permissive provenance or ignored leaks.
rust_safety_extensions: Overflowing allocation-byte multiplication and publication beyond logical/physical capacity return Failure. The native raw setter alone accepts any numeric value; later uninitialized/out-of-bounds reads or destruction are not reproduced.
A test creates a larger retained stride only to prove Rust publication rejection before access; no equivalent undefined native memory access is compiled.
Retained/live copyParameters destinations are rejected, preserving existing owned allocator/layout metadata. This is a constrained binding, not full native retained-block semantics.
remaining_partial_parity: copyDate and replaceAt remain deferred. Native incomplete copied-block leaks/trivial-copy dispatch and three-way assignment/move_if_noexcept/destruct+construct dispatch are not modeled by blanket Rust Clone or assignment.
copy_parameters does not yet cover existing allocated blocks, forgotten live slots or allocator rebinding on those blocks.

Constructor closures produce Rust values before ptr::write; arbitrary address-dependent/in-place C++ constructors, partially written byte observations after constructor failure and implicit custom C++ move hooks are not claimed.
destroy_at requires Drop not to unwind for native noexcept parity; Rust panic versus native termination behavior is not changed.

Raw allocator null/zero-size/OOM behavior follows the existing allocator abstraction; the16-row fixture verifies successful nonzero allocation and constructor failure, not every platform allocation edge.
Previous generic move, same-container alias, cursor identity/comparison, and pointer-vector allocation-policy limitations remain as recorded in earlier scoped receipts.
Six bounded declaration adapters and sixteen supplemental rows do not establish whole DynamicArray/template or global API parity.
